message: No detected untrusted source handling: All data is read from local file paths only (pd.read_csv with local paths); no remote sources are used, so no integrity verification or authentication is present.
No detected label flipping detection: No code checks label distributions, validates label values against an expected set, or uses any label-noise detection tool before training.

No detected data poisoning defenses: The only data cleaning performed is replacing NaN values with 0.0; there are no outlier detection, statistical anomaly checks, or suspicious-input filtering mechanisms.

No detected model integrity verification: The code instantiates models directly from sklearn/xgboost/catboost constructors with hardcoded hyperparameters and does not load any serialized/pretrained model weights, so there is no integrity verification implemented.

No detected label distribution validation: The code prints class counts after resampling via DataController.count_classes_size but does not validate or assert any expected label distribution before training begins.
No detected backdoor or trigger detection: There is no activation analysis, trigger detection, or any other backdoor defense mechanism anywhere in the training pipeline.
No detected differential privacy: The code uses standard sklearn, XGBoost, and CatBoost classifiers with no differential privacy libraries or mechanisms applied.
No detected adversarial robustness testing: No adversarial robustness libraries (Foolbox, ART, etc.) or attack methods (FGSM, PGD) are imported or invoked anywhere in the code.

No detected metric tampering protection: Although a train/test split is performed, there is no isolation of a held-out test set from training data beyond a basic split, no signing or hashing of evaluation data, and results are written to CSV without integrity checks or multiple independent verification paths.

No detected input sanitization: The code only replaces NaN values with 0.0 and checks for empty DataFrames/missing files, but performs no input shape, range, or schema validation before passing data to the model.
No detected output bounds checks: Model predictions are passed directly to scoring functions without any NaN guards, probability bounds checks, or threshold validation on the outputs.

No detected prompt injection defenses: The models used (XGBoost, CatBoost, LogisticRegression, etc.) are tabular ML classifiers, not LLMs, so prompt injection defenses are not applicable and none are implemented.
